newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to off.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.200 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts look for further weakness in live cattle futures after June declined to its lowest level in nearly six weeks with declining boxed beef values and easier live market projections selling factors. Fed cattle are expected to trade down another $1 per cwt to $63 next week, they said.
However, other analysts consider futures oversold and see the market near major weekly support on the charts.

Feeder cattle futures were exptected to continue the recent easier trend and trade steady to lower following the declining CME feeder cattle index and higher trending corn futures. Losses in live cattle futures and heavy feedlot cattle supplies should also weigh on the market, they said.
However, underlying support could again be cited on expectations of tight feeder cattle supplies into the fall period, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.12 at $77.48 per cwt.
